# core/aesgcm.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/aesgcm.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

Authenticated encryption with AES-128 in Galois/Counter
Mode (NIST SP 800-38D) with a 96-bit nonce and a 128-bit tag, as
TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 uses it.

What is proved: every access is in bounds, nothing leaks, a sealed message
is 16 bytes longer than its plaintext, and `gcm_open` returns `Some` only
after the tag has been compared in full. Not proved: that the output is
GCM's (the tests check NIST's vectors and messages sealed by OpenSSL, and a
tampered byte in every position), or that the code is constant time: the
S-box lookups of core/aes.bastio depend on the key and data (see there),
and the multiplication in GF(2^128) is by shifts and masks, bit by bit,
with no branch on a secret.

A nonce must never be used twice with one key.

`import "core/aesgcm.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/aes.bastio](core-aes.md), [core/endian.bastio](core-endian.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`gcm_seal`](#gcm_seal) | Encrypts `plain` and authenticates it and `aad`. |
| [`gcm_open`](#gcm_open) | Checks the tag at the end of `sealed` and, if it is right, decrypts. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `gcm_seal`

```bastio
fn gcm_seal(key: &Bytes, nonce: &Bytes, aad: &Bytes, plain: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(key) == 16 && blen(nonce) == 12 && blen(aad) < 274877906944 && blen(plain) < 274877906944
  ensures blen(result) == blen(plain) + 16
```

Encrypts `plain` and authenticates it and `aad`: the ciphertext followed
by the 16-byte tag.

Example:

```bastio
let key = balloc(16);
let nonce = balloc(12);
let aad = balloc(0);
let plain = bfrom("hello");
let sealed = gcm_seal(key, nonce, aad, plain);
let n = blen(sealed);
bfree(sealed);
bfree(plain);
bfree(aad);
bfree(nonce);
bfree(key);
if n != 21 { return 1; }
```

### `gcm_open`

```bastio
fn gcm_open(key: &Bytes, nonce: &Bytes, aad: &Bytes, sealed: &Bytes) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires blen(key) == 16 && blen(nonce) == 12 && blen(aad) < 274877906944 && blen(sealed) < 274877906944
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) + 16 == blen(sealed)
```

Checks the tag at the end of `sealed` and, if it is right, decrypts: the
plaintext. `None` for a message shorter than a tag, or one whose tag, data
or `aad` was changed.

Example:

```bastio
let key = balloc(16);
let nonce = balloc(12);
let aad = balloc(0);
let plain = bfrom("x");
let mut sealed = gcm_seal(key, nonce, aad, plain);
bset(&mut sealed, 0, bget(sealed, 0) ^ 1);     // flip a bit
let mut refused = true;
match gcm_open(key, nonce, aad, sealed) {
  Option::Some(p) => { refused = false; bfree(p); },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(sealed);
bfree(plain);
bfree(aad);
bfree(nonce);
bfree(key);
if !refused { return 1; }
```

## Internals

### `gcm_mul`

```bastio
fn gcm_mul(x: &Bytes, h: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(x) == 16 && blen(h) == 16
  ensures blen(result) == 16
```

Internal: the product of the 16-byte blocks `x` and `h` in GF(2^128), with
the bit order of SP 800-38D (the first bit is the most significant).

### `gcm_absorb`

```bastio
fn gcm_absorb(y: &mut Bytes, h: &Bytes, data: &Bytes)
  requires blen(y) == 16 && blen(h) == 16 && blen(data) < 274877906944
  ensures blen(y) == 16
```

Internal: folds `data`, a block of 16 bytes at a time (the last one padded
with zeros), into the GHASH state `y`.

### `gcm_ghash`

```bastio
fn gcm_ghash(h: &Bytes, aad: &Bytes, ct: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(h) == 16 && blen(aad) < 274877906944 && blen(ct) < 274877906944
  ensures blen(result) == 16
```

Internal: GHASH of `aad` and the ciphertext `ct`, with their lengths in bits.

### `gcm_ctr`

```bastio
fn gcm_ctr(a: &Aes128, nonce: &Bytes, start: u64, data: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires aes_ok(a) && blen(nonce) == 12 && blen(data) < 274877906944
  ensures blen(result) == blen(data)
```

Internal: `data` xor the AES-CTR keystream that starts at the counter
block `nonce || 00 00 00 start`.

### `gcm_tag`

```bastio
fn gcm_tag(a: &Aes128, nonce: &Bytes, aad: &Bytes, ct: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires aes_ok(a) && blen(nonce) == 12 && blen(aad) < 274877906944 && blen(ct) < 274877906944
  ensures blen(result) == 16
```

Internal: the tag over `aad` and the ciphertext `ct`.
